notes:
T906 (why do 271 briefs violate a rule the dispatcher enforces?) — answered: because the rule was enforced at bin/dispatch only, and rows are CREATED by `managent add`/`suggest`, which enforced nothing. Measured fresh on the live corpus: 285 of 825 briefs with a managent header (34.5%) carry a title over 40 chars — worst 139 chars, T407 (the brief's cited 271/726 (37%) is directionally confirmed; the worst-139 datum reproduces exactly; denominators differ because the corpus is live and the brief's population definition differs). FIXED: the title gate now lives at REGISTRATION — `managent add` (both the named-id and --auto mint paths) and `managent suggest` refuse a bundle whose title line is missing or whose title portion exceeds 40 chars, naming the title, its length and the limit; a missing title line is refused for THAT reason with a DIFFERENT message than the over-long case (two failure modes, two messages). The title PORTION grammar (`# <id> — <title>`, any non-whitespace id token) is SHARED with bin/dispatch's re-assert (dispatch's title_re relaxed from `T\d+` to `\S+` for the id), so the two entry points cannot disagree about what a title is. bin/dispatch KEEPS its check as a cheap re-assert (decided and defended): pre-T906 rows (the 285 over-length briefs, incl. the 271 the brief measured) and bundles edited after registration are only ever caught there, and it already reads the same title line. The title is RECORDED on the row at registration (`title` store field, serialized/parsed, shown by `managent show`) so a deleted brief cannot erase the row's name; legacy rows parse null (never guessed). No historical titles were rewritten (fix forward; a row's title is part of the record) — the actionable offender list for still-dispatchable rows is findings/T906-title-gate-offenders.json: 9 rows (8 over-40: T535/T709/T715/T798/T825 + the DARGUS/DCLAIM/DRPLAY duties; 1 dangling bundle: T735), with a suggested short title each for the seat to apply. Corpus-wide backfill of the stored title field for legacy rows is a follow-up (report, do not sprawl).

TEST-FIRST: tools/regression-title-gate.sh written before the fix and shown RED against the pre-fix deployed binary (arms 1/3/4/5/6 fail exactly as the brief measured: 60-char title registered, no-title-line bundle registered, 41-char registered, suggest accepted the 41-char slug, --auto registered) then GREEN after (all 6 arms, incl. the null controls: store carries the title, show names it; the missing-title message is distinct; exactly 40 passes / exactly 41 refused). Red and green transcripts in findings/T906-title-gate-context.json. Wired into `zig build test` in build.zig.

RELATED FIXES (the gate's blast radius on the suite, each verified): regression-managent-store-write-utf8.sh fixture titles were over 40 chars (T700 55, T701 44) and are now legal; regression-dispatch.sh arms 17-18 seed the bad-title row DIRECTLY into the store (the pre-gate population) instead of via add, which the gate now correctly refuses, so dispatch's re-assert is still exercised; regression-managent-landmark.sh's real-corpus sweep classifies refusals by gate (title vs landmark) so the 285 over-length corpus briefs are not mislabeled as malformed landmark declarations; regression-managent-lanes.sh / store-pollution.sh fixtures gained a `—` separator (their `# T<n> bundle` headings have no title line). dispatch-verification, dispatch-caps, subagent-prompt, lock, status-json, directive-kill, claim-lifecycle, window-resilience, watch-fleet, fleet-keeper, argus-doctor, task-id-archive, battery-baselines: verified baseline-red with identical failure signatures (pre-existing, not this wave).

SUITE: `zig build test` end-to-end — 114/132 steps succeeded (17 failed); 1369/1370 tests passed (1 skipped). Failing steps: 13 sh scripts that are baseline-red in sweep-pre (verified identical signatures), regression-precommit.sh + regression-ollama-dispatcher.sh (SWEEP-CONTRACT-excluded ambient classes), and TWO zig test steps (managent + vb_fixpoint) that die in the build-runner `--listen` protocol with EndOfStream while every test passes — PROVEN NOT THIS WAVE by a minimal-build isolation: a tiny build.zig running ONLY the managent test step fails identically with HEAD's committed main.zig (no T906 code) and with the index version (no T906, foreign staged hunks) as with mine; the T635 OS-entropy draw test's stderr output precedes the death in all three; zero assertion failures (1369/1370). vb_fixpoint is a module this wave never touched and dies the same way. Reported for the Orchestrator: the suite's zig test steps are unreliable under the build runner on this host with zig 0.16.0_1 (T880's earlier clean suite notwithstanding); the sh-script sweep is the reliable gate.

DECISION — dispatch keeps its re-assert (the brief asked to choose and defend): (1) the 285 pre-gate over-length briefs are only ever caught at dispatch; registration cannot retroactively gate them; (2) the bundle FILE is mutable after registration — a title edited in after add is caught at dispatch (the same file it already reads for landmark/directive checks, so the marginal cost is zero); (3) removing the dispatch check would re-create the T753/T880 path for pre-gate rows. This is not 'two gates for one rule' as the defect describes it: registration is the gate, dispatch is a stale-input detector for the historical population and post-registration drift.

Landmark: advances L1 (the dashboard tells the truth) — a title the dashboard displays is now legal at the moment the row exists; the 37% over-length population stops growing, the seat has the actionable offender list, and the 285 historical titles remain the record (fix forward). What remains: a corpus-wide backfill of the stored `title` field for legacy rows (report, do not sprawl), and the fleet's own decision to apply the 9 suggested re-titles from findings/T906-title-gate-offenders.json (several offender rows are held by other rows — do not edit them from this task).
